solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like specialised equipment for speaking an ancient language

indicators.note: speaking means we want what the phrase sounds like when said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: like = as, and specialised equipment = tech, kit for technical work

explanation.surface: Someone describes special gear needed to speak a long-dead tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like it introduces a comparison; it is a word swap for as.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec is a common name for Nahuatl, the tongue of the pre-conquest Mexican empire.

clue.text: Queen and wizard involved in extra destructive event

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so these pieces go within another word

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen and a wizard caught up in an especially devastating occurrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra destructive' reads as one phrase, but extra is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the prophesied final battle, used for any catastrophic, world-ending conflict.

clue.text: Item that's baked without sugar finally rubbish

indicators.note: without signals something going missing from the word before it
finally restricts the removal to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: a tart is a baked pastry

explanation.surface: A sugar-free bake ends up as garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is cheap, shoddy goods, junk.

clue.text: Hamburger maybe covered in extremely crunchy fruit?

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by what follows, which goes around it
extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: a man from Hamburg is addressed as Herr, German for Mr

explanation.surface: A burger, perhaps, coated in a crisp fruity layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is a native of Hamburg, a German gentleman, not a burger.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small stone fruit; the question mark covers the fruit tree or colour.

clue.text: Pub employee's dog biting front of Eagles record?

indicators.note: a dog biting something holds it in its jaws, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a barker is a dog, one that barks

indicators.note: front of means only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A barman's dog chews up the front of an Eagles disc.
explanation.walkthrough: A barker is any dog that barks; the record is an extended-play single.
explanation.definitionFit: A barkeeper is the person who serves drinks behind a bar.

clue.text: Fantastic comedy film subject inspiring poor over time

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one word draws another inside it

parts.note: Monty Python's Life of Brian is about Brian
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A great comedy film's topic inspires the poor across time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the earlier part sits above what follows. The film is Monty Python's Life of Brian.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant and fantastic are both informal ways to say excellent.

clue.text: Fix hat when leaving a fair

parts.note: to rig is to fix a result dishonestly

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the named letter goes out of the word

explanation.surface: Adjusting your hat on the way out of a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fair' looks like a funfair; fair is the definition, and a is the letter removed from HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and fair both mean just or proper.

clue.text: Asked, in French, about splitting some money

indicators.note: splitting means driving into the middle of something, so it sits inside

parts.note: a quid is a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone asked in French about splitting a sum of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Enquired is a past-tense verb meaning asked a question.

clue.text: Elephant and rat swimming in our home

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: An elephant and a rat swimming about in the place we live.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the planet where humanity lives, so it is home to us all.

clue.text: Regret carrying large measuring stick

indicators.note: carrying means holding something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Sorry to be hauling a big yardstick about.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule, or ruler, is a straight strip used to measure lengths.

clue.text: Bearing second article — jewellery

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A list of a bearing, a second article and some jewellery, like a catalogue entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second article' tempts you to read two articles; second is a moment, as in 'just a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing a child and caring for it is mothering, acting as a parent.

clue.text: Some birds cower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small game birds, the plural being the same as the singular
second meaning: to shrink back in fear

explanation.surface: A few birds cringe in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names small game birds, plural unchanged, and the verb means to flinch or lose courage.

clue.text: Officer's getting young person's vehicle when everyone's out?

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer; the 's gives the S
a trike is a child's tricycle

explanation.surface: An army officer gets a kid's tricycle while everyone else has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is in the sense of workers out on strike, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A general strike is a stoppage by workers across all industries at once, so everybody has walked out.

clue.text: Pinch pure metal finally, then reportedly pinch an alloy

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the last letters of the two words

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word that follows is chosen for its sound

explanation.surface: Steal some pure metal and then steal an alloy, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick and pinch are both British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel steel is steel alloyed with nickel for extra toughness.

clue.text: He attracts bats with some difficulty

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man lures the flying mammals, though not easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' reads as the animals; it is the adjective for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: At a stretch is an idiom for only just possible, with effort.

clue.text: Avoid a very low score

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dodge or evade
second meaning: a cricket score of nought

explanation.surface: Advice to stay clear of a dismal result.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter out without scoring has made a duck, a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means dodge, and as a cricket noun it is a batter's nil score.

clue.text: Those in charge of viral image including a horse and cart ultimately

indicators.note: including means one word takes the others inside it

parts.note: a meme is an image shared virally online
a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The bosses of a viral picture showing a horse and cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is shortened to 'n, as in rock 'n' roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Management is the collective term for the people who run a business.

clue.text: Amazed when One Direction gets into a fight?

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrum

explanation.surface: Stunned when the boy band One Direction start a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a pop group, but here the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, so overwhelmed with amazement.

clue.text: Friends upset over wicked-sounding guitar technique

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the word from the bottom
sounding means the word is chosen for how it is pronounced

explanation.surface: Mates are annoyed by an evil-sounding way to play guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the reversed pals above the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap bass is a way of playing bass guitar by slapping and popping the strings.

clue.text: Landlord following old writer's public correspondence

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed after the others

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing tool
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A landlord comes after an aged author's open published letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlord is one who lets property, read whimsically as a 'letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: An open letter is addressed to someone but published for everyone to read.

clue.text: Eye piece from virtual assistant swivelling around

indicators.note: something swivelling round turns to face the other way, so the word is read back to front

explanation.surface: An eyepiece comes out of a voice assistant spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured ring in the eye, one part of it.

clue.text: Half a dog's allocation is fruit?

wordplay.note: a dog is allotted four paws, so half its share is two of them

explanation.surface: Half of what a dog is given turns out to be fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allocation' suggests food rations; it is the dog's set of four feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawpaw is a tropical fruit, another name for papaya; the question mark flags the punning route.

clue.text: Possibly miss standing in party heels with cup getting drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young woman at a party in heels gets drunk from her cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman, but it is the schoolroom title for a female teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply teacher covers for an absent regular one, and might be addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Book lender ignoring railway sign

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A book lender pays no attention to a railway notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railway sign' looks like one thing; sign is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Mother ship's bulk

explanation.surface: The size of the mother ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass and bulk both mean the size or quantity of matter in something.

clue.text: Running near a stadium

indicators.note: running suggests a mixture that has run, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Jogging close to a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or shows, much like a stadium.

clue.text: Plan put Berlin in a pickle

indicators.note: in a pickle means in a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A scheme left the German capital in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed design or scheme for something to be made.

clue.text: Not well drilled in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the word is needed, a run of its letters

parts.note: the run of letters after its first two

explanation.surface: Someone poorly prepared only partly through training.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill means sick, in poor health.

clue.text: Drinking beers, closely follow persuasive argument

indicators.note: something drinking takes liquid inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to stalk someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: After a few pints, someone tails a person with a convincing case.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales talk is the patter a seller uses to persuade a buyer.

clue.text: Mostly fairly quiet like Lloyd-George

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: well in the sense of quite, as in well capable
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A description of a rather softly spoken historical statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lloyd George, British prime minister 1916–22, was raised in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd George was a Welshman, so the adjective describes him by nationality.
